subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and which default exclusions, protected paths, and exclude-file trust rules should be part of the core CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but defaults and protected recovery paths decide the balance between backup size, sensitive-file avoidance, and restorable archives.

options.title: Review the linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, conflicts, and real proof before landing or narrowing it.

options.title: Narrow to explicit custom excludes
options.body: Accept `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` first while deferring smart defaults until restore completeness and sensitive-file policy are clearer.

options.title: Decline native excludes for now
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document current scope, and direct optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review the linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, conflicts, and real proof before landing or narrowing it.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras is tied to the original backup CLI review/ownership trail and helper refactor history, making them the strongest product-boundary routing candidate from current evidence.
